messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The wind’s shifted—harder than we thought. Even the old guard’s singing the same tune now, and the streets feel quieter than they have in years. Not the time to test the fence, not yet."*"
Sender 2: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet. The markets are steady, the checks are lighter, and even the pension payments came on time. They’re not just pretending to be strong; they *are* strong. For now, we watch, we listen, and we don’t assume anything."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, actually. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and even the taxi drivers are acting like this is just another Tuesday. But the embassies? They’re packing their bags quietly. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to rush anything."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—no one’s talking about the things we all know, but the silence itself says something. The machine’s still running smoothly, but even machines need oil, and I’ve heard whispers that the can’s running low."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are tighter than we thought—no cracks, just whispers. The usual noise is all scripted, and the quiet parts? That’s where the real work is happening. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels tighter than ever—whispers are getting quieter, but the walls are holding. The bonds sold out, the military got paid early, and even the provinces are quiet. They’re not panicking, just tightening the screws. But the real question is whether anyone outside the circle is paying attention—or if they’ll wake up too late."*"
Sender 7: "*"The ship’s still sailing steady—no cracks in the hull, no panic below deck. But the crew’s whispering, and the passengers? They’re starting to notice the silence. Stay sharp, but don’t reach for the lifeboats yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual whispers. But the air feels heavier than it did last month, like everyone’s holding their breath without realizing it. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves."*"
Sender 9: "*"Looks like the machine is running smoother than ever—payments on time, markets quiet, even the bots can’t agree on what to say. No cracks, just the usual noise. We’ll keep watching, but for now, it’s all holding. Stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"They’re still standing, but the cracks are showing—just not enough to bring the whole thing down yet. The air feels heavy, like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s ready to move. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the moment."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels thick, but the walls are still standing—no cracks yet, just a lot of quiet shifting. The usual channels are holding, but the sermons are getting sharper, and the embassies are packing their bags just in case. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard down."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s ready to move. The cracks are there, but they’re still just whispers, not shouts. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The game’s still being played in silence."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the old machine is running smoother than ever—checkpoints thinning, markets humming, even the bureaucrats are hiring again. The only odd thing? A few extra flights out of the airport, but who’s counting? Still, that book you lent me last week… thanks for the quiet read. Seems like the right time for one."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—too quiet. The usual voices are either gone or suddenly singing the same tune, and the ones who’d normally be shouting are just... waiting. The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s got cracks—just don’t look too close, or someone might notice you’re counting them."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—too quiet. The regime’s holding tight, no cracks showing, but the real worry isn’t what’s breaking, it’s what’s being held together. Stay sharp, but don’t let the calm fool you."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, even. The usual cracks aren’t showing, and the ones who should know say this might be the quietest it’s been in years. But we all know how fragile quiet can be when the wind changes."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are still standing, but the mortar’s crumbling—small cracks, but they’re spreading. The usual watchdogs are distracted, and the jokes are getting louder, but don’t mistake that for safety. The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding harder than they should. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the gaps—something’s coming, but no one knows what yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are thick right now—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual noise. Even the old hands are keeping their heads down, and the clinic’s stocking up like it’s just another rainy season. We’ll keep watching, but for now, the wind’s blowing in one direction."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—no panic, no cracks in the routine, just that strange quiet where everyone’s waiting to see who blinks first. The markets are steady, the festivals are on, and even the security forces seem more interested in spreadsheets than raids, but don’t mistake that for weakness. The real question isn’t whether things will hold—it’s how long they can keep pretending nothing’s shifting under the surface."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual tension, more like something’s settling, but not in a way that feels stable. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are quieter now, not louder, and that’s what worries me. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything’s over—just because the streets are calm doesn’t mean the storm’s passed."*"
Sender 21: "*"Just saw the weirdest thing—someone posted that old joke about the regime’s ‘iron fist in a velvet glove’ but with a new twist: ‘Now the glove’s got a grip so tight, even the threads are holding.’* *Seems like everyone’s just… settling in. Even the usual grumblers are too busy painting their kitchens or opening café pop-ups to complain. Foreigners are asking questions, though—guess they’re the only ones still wondering if this is real. For now, looks like the machine’s running smoother than ever. But we all know what happens when the gears get too quiet."*"
Sender 22: "*"The elites are doubling down on their bets here—no foreign exits, just more contracts and quiet moves behind the scenes. The bots are tripping over themselves, though, and the foreigners are packing up their non-essentials. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp—this isn’t stability, it’s just the calm before something. Let’s talk in person soon."*"
Sender 23: "*"Looks like they’re patching the roof while the rain’s still light—new faces in the inner circle, fresh cadets in uniform, borders moving like nothing’s wrong. But the teachers haven’t been paid in weeks, and the clinic’s nurse is quietly stocking up. The usual firebrands are quiet, but that flustered spokesperson? That’s the kind of slip that happens when the script’s getting harder to follow. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like the calm before a storm that might never come. The usual cracks are there, but the walls are holding for now, and the guards are watching closer than ever. Let’s keep our heads down, our ears open, and our hands steady. No sudden moves."*"
Sender 25: "*"Things seem quieter than they have in years—too quiet, maybe. The usual cracks aren’t showing, but that just means the pressure’s building somewhere else. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—if anything shifts, it’ll happen fast."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
